records.name: Hilda
records.facts_used: Hilda: The family contains Germanic hild-, battle, also given by Siliņš as Old High German hiltja. Hilda occurs both independently and as a short form of longer compounds. The derivatives’ full forms and their dates remain distinct. Siliņš’s dictionary dates the use of Hilda: the last quarter of the nineteenth century. Its calendar year is 1915. This records use of the particular name in Latvia. The entry cannot automatically be transferred to similar spellings or treated as the moment the entire name family originated.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Siliņš p 154 exact hiltja and Hilda under Hildegarde/Brunhilde; ownlastquarter 19 c/calendar 1915.

records.name: Drovydė
records.facts_used: Drovydė: The Lithuanian compound contains dro-, connected with drovus, shy or modest, and vyd-, connected with seeing. The feminine form corresponds to Drovydas. Explaining the separate stems does not require one invented literal sentence. The 1964 calendar reprinted in Salys’s 1983 volume gives Drovydė (Drova) on 17 December. This is a concrete printed example of the form’s use. Its position in the historical calendar need not match every modern calendar and is not the name’s invention date.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Original Salys December 17 exact Drovydė; Pakerys PDF 2/printed 91 explicit Dróvydas–Dróvydė. Mantgailas is not silently equated with neighbouring Mantigaila.

records.name: Olimpija
records.facts_used: Olimpija: The name family is linked to Greek Olympos, the name of Mount Olympus. Its further origin and meaning are not securely established. The secure connection is with the place name and its family, without an invented translation of the ancient root. Page 240 of the 1983 study gives Olimpija in a separate personal-name entry. This is dated evidence for the exact form in scholarly work. Publication does not mark a first birth record or the name’s invention.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Original Salys PDF 255/printed 240 distinguishes ONOlympia and PNOlympia rows; accepted personal-name row, not just place. Unknown remote place-name meaning remains unspecified.

records.name: Raili
records.facts_used: Raili: The name belongs to the Rahel/Rachel family from Hebrew rachel, ewe. A specific animal word stands behind the historical name. This is not a description of a modern bearer’s character invented from similar sounds. Page 18 of Mägiste’s 1929 name list gives Raili with a Finnish-calendar reference. This is specific dated evidence for the local form. The dictionary’s publication year is not the name’s invention date or a first birth record.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Original Mägiste PDF 20/printed 18 exact Raili(sm.Alm.); Estonian-specific Rahelshortening explicit in Leole and curated Raili. Finnishdictionary’s additional proposals are not generalized to all Estonianbearers.
